landmarks.name: Zuma Rock
landmarks.writeup: A natural monolith located in Niger State, often called the 'Gateway to Abuja' and known for its unique face-like features.

wiki.extract: Zuma Rock is a large natural monolith, or inselberg, an igneous intrusion composed of gabbro and granodiorite and of Precambrian age, located in Madalla, a town in Niger State, Nigeria. It is situated in the west of Nigeria's capital, Abuja, along the main road from Abuja to Kaduna, off Madalla, and is sometimes referred to as the "Gateway to Abuja from Suleja". Zuma Rock rises approximately 725 metres (2,379 ft) above sea level. It was once thought to be in the Federal Capital Territory but is actually located at the upper end of Madalla, a rural settlement in Suleja Local Government Area of Niger State.

landmarks.name: Olumo Rock
landmarks.writeup: A massive outcrop of granite rocks in Abeokuta, Ogun State, historically used as a fortress by the Egba people.

wiki.extract: Olumo Rock is a mountain in south-western Nigeria. It is located in the city of Abeokuta, Ogun State, and was normally used as a natural fortress during inter-tribal warfare in the 19th century. Its patron spirit is venerated in the Yoruba religion as an orisha. In addition, Olumo Rock is an important paleontological archaeological site that has yielded an outstanding collection of stone tools such as hand axes, artificially shaped spherical rocks, pick-like tools and hammer rocks, dating back approximately 1.5 million years. The name olumo is the combination of two words: "olu" which means god/deity, and "mo" which means moulded.

landmarks.name: National Mosque, Abuja
landmarks.writeup: An important religious site and architectural landmark in Nigeria's capital city.

wiki.extract: The Abuja National Mosque, also known as the Nigerian National Mosque, is the national mosque of Nigeria, located in the capital city, Abuja. The mosque was built in 1984 and is open to the non-Muslim public, except during congregational prayers.

landmarks.name: Aso Rock
landmarks.writeup: A large rock formation in Abuja, near the Nigerian Presidential Complex and National Assembly.

wiki.extract: The State House is the workplace and official residence of the President of Nigeria since 1991, when Nigeria moved its capital from Lagos to Abuja. It is located at Yakubu Gowon Crescent, Asokoro District, Abuja in the Federal Capital Territory of Nigeria. The Aso Rock Villa hosts the offices of the President and Vice President and it is the seat of the Executive Arm of the Federal Government of Nigeria. The Aso Rock Villa is the most protected presidential state house in Africa. It is heavily protected by the Presidential Guards Brigade and the State Security Service.

landmarks.name: Obudu Mountain Resort
landmarks.writeup: A scenic resort in Cross River State known for its cable cars, waterfalls, and temperate climate.

wiki.extract: Obanliku Mountain Resort is a ranch and resort on the Obudu Plateau in Cross River State, Nigeria.

cultural_events.name: Durbar Festival
cultural_events.writeup: A traditional festival celebrated mainly in Northern Nigeria featuring horse parades, music, and cultural displays.

wiki.extract: The Durbar festival is an annual cultural, religious and equestrian festival, celebrated as a core part of Hausa culture in Arewa. Durbar has existed for centuries in the Hausa Kingdoms, and is a paramount part of Hausa cultural rites, tradition, and history.

cultural_events.name: Eyo Festival
cultural_events.writeup: A Lagos-based festival involving masquerades dressed in white, honoring the memory of important Lagos figures.

wiki.extract: The Eyo Festival, otherwise known as the Adamu Orisha Play, is a Yoruba festival unique to Lagos, Nigeria and has a strong historical footing in Iperu-Remo, a town in Ikenne Local Government, Ogun State. In modern times, it is presented by the people of Lagos as a tourist event. Due to the history of its development, it is traditionally performed on Lagos Island. A notable festival date was in 2000 commemorating Justice G.B.A. Coker, a Lagos high chief, the Olori Adimu and the Olori Eyo of the Adimu Eyo cultural masquerade. Chief Kabiru Adeshina Oshodi, a high chief who is a member of the Eyo Laba is the Heads of all Eyo masquerades in Lagos making him the Olori Eleyo of Lagos.

cultural_events.name: New Yam Festival
cultural_events.writeup: An annual celebration by the Igbo people marking the end of the farming season and the harvest of new yams.

wiki.extract: Igbo Yam Festivals refers to the multiple annual cultural festival by the Igbo people, held at the end of the rainy season in early August to mark the first harvest of yams and to offer thanksgiving for a successful agricultural year.

cultural_events.name: Calabar Carnival
cultural_events.writeup: Known as Africa's biggest street party, this December event features music, dance, and cultural exhibitions.

wiki.extract: Calabar Carnival also known as "Carnival Calabar" is an annual carnival held in Cross River State, Nigeria. Colloquially entitled Africa's Biggest Street Party, the carnival holds every December and was declared by the then governor of Cross River State, Mr. Donald Duke as an activity to mark Christmas celebration yearly. He said his vision for creating the festival was to make Cross-River a home of tourism and hospitality in Nigeria and Africa. The quality of the festival has grown over the years making it Nigeria's biggest carnival and an internationally recognized festival. It used to be a month-long event that began on the 1st of December, until the former governor of the state, Benedict Ayade reduced it to two weeks after he was elected. During the 2017 carnival, Former governor Benedict Ayade said in his speech that the carnival is to showcase Africa as the richest continent and a blessed place where the young ones should be proud to belong. The carnival has always been entertaining and colourful as different competitions take place and huge cash prizes are won. Calabar which is also known by the name Canaan City, is a city in southern Nigeria. Calabar is actually the capital city of Cross River State. Calabar sits adjacent to the Calabar and Great Kwa Rivers and Falls as well as the creeks of the Cross River. according to Ojoi Ekpenyong, the managing director of the tourism bureau, disclosed that the event hosted over 248,000 visitors.

food_writeup: Nigerian cuisine is diverse and flavorful, featuring staples like jollof rice, pounded yam, egusi soup, suya (spiced grilled meat), and akara (bean cakes). Meals often combine rich spices, vegetables, and proteins reflecting the country's ethnic diversity.
brief_history: Nigeria gained independence from British colonial rule in 1960. It has a history marked by diverse ethnic groups, military coups, civil war (1967-1970), and a transition to democratic governance since 1999. It is Africa's most populous country and a major oil producer.

commentary.inflation_management: Nigeria's inflation has been structurally high and is now in crisis territory. It averaged 8-13% from 2006 to 2015 under a managed naira, then the 2016 devaluation pushed it to 15.7-16.5% in 2016-17. The central bank's multiple-exchange-rate regime and deficit financing kept it at 11-19% through 2022. The 2023 reforms were the breaking point: subsidy removal and the June 2023 naira float sent inflation to 24.7% in 2023 and a series high of 33.2% in 2024, with 23.0% projected for 2025. The central bank has hiked rates aggressively, but with food inflation far higher than headline and the naira still adjusting, expectations remain unanchored. There is no formal inflation target; policy is crisis management.
commentary.debt_management: Nigeria's debt was negligible after the 2005 Paris Club deal: 5.2% of GDP in 2008, the series low. The 2014 oil crash ended the era of oil-financed budgets, and the government borrowed steadily to fund deficits: debt reached 39.3% of GDP in 2024, the series high, easing to a projected 36.3% in 2025. The ratio flatters the problem: with revenues among the world's lowest as a share of GDP, debt service consumes an enormous share of government income, and much borrowing has been expensive domestic debt. The 2023 reforms (subsidy removal, naira float) improved the fiscal arithmetic, but sustainability depends on raising non-oil revenues, which has eluded every government.

key_events.event: Oil price crash: GDP in USD terms peaked at $811.1bn (2014), then collapsed; 2016 recession.
Muhammadu Buhari won the presidency, ending 16 years of PDP rule.
COVID-19 and oil crash; #EndSARS protests shook the country.
Naira redesign fiasco ahead of elections; Bola Tinubu won the disputed 2023 vote.
May 29, 2023: Tinubu removed the fuel subsidy; June 2023: naira floated and FX rates unified; inflation surged to 33.2% in 2024.
Dangote refinery began operations, promising to end fuel imports.

commentary.outlook_next_decade: The base case is painful adjustment: if the 2023 reforms hold, inflation should fall to single digits and growth recover on refining and gas; if they are reversed, the crisis resumes. Upside is large (Dangote refinery, tax reform, oil production recovery); downside is political: reforms have made Tinubu deeply unpopular and the 2027 election looms. Uncertainty is high: Nigeria has started reforms many times, but never finished them.
commentary.caveat: Outlook is an analytical assessment as of October 2026, not a forecast. 2025 figures are IMF estimates/projections.
